title: Crestbridge retail partner playbook (scratch)
body:
Purpose / quick goal:
 - Capture signal on Crestbridge (midmarket retail platform) fit for a co-delivered in-store AI assistant pilot.
 - Draft outreach + objections, list stakeholders, sketch pilot scope and success metrics, prepare call prep bullets.

Quick snapshot (public + skimmed intel)
 - Crestbridge: commerce platform for independent retail chains (POS + catalog + in-store digital assistants). HQ SF. ~180 engineers, Series C (2023). Customers: regional grocers, specialty apparel groups.
 - Recent product push: "In-store discovery" (beta launched Q4 2024) — aims to provide staff-facing search + shopper kiosks.
 - Technical signals: uses microservices on k8s, AWS, RBAC via Okta, stores PII in encrypted RDS. Likely ok with hosted API if PII not sent; otherwise Dedicated or Private.

Primary contacts (to validate)
 - Dir Product, Search & Discovery: Elena Morales — owns in-store product roadmap (likely DM).
 - Head of Eng (platform): Tom Greenwood — evaluates infra, data governance.
 - Solutions Architect: Priya Khatri — hands-on for pilots & integration.
 - Retail Ops lead (pilot customer champion): Aaron Lim.

Pain points we can solve / hypotheses
 - Current retrieval/search: slow tail latencies for long product catalogs (bad in-kiosk UX).
 - They want contextual, brand-safe recommendations + quick SKU lookup for staff.
 - Cost sensitivity for inference at scale in-store (thousands of small requests).
 - Need predictable SLA for peak weekend traffic.

Potential Redwood value props to highlight (short)
 - Predictable per-request latency (can show P50/P95 numbers on comparable workloads).
 - Dedicated capacity / private deployment options for PII-sensitive flows.
 - Built-in batching + KV caching reduces token/unit cost for repeated queries (relevant for catalog lookups).
 - Rollouts + canary for feature flagging and fallback to smaller model when capacity/latency constraints.

Pilot hypothesis / scope (2–4 week pilot)
 - Goal: reduce avg kiosk query latency from ~550ms to <200ms P95 and improve successful SKU resolution by 15% over baseline.
 - Scope: integrate redwood-hosted or dedicated inference for staff-facing SKU lookup and short Q&A (no full PII). Minimal UI hook in existing kiosk.
 - Data: sample catalog + search telemetry (~2M SKUs example? need exact size).
 - Success metrics: P95 latency, SKU resolution rate, tokens/cost per 1k queries, ops overhead to run.

Integration options (pros/cons)
 - Hosted Redwood API: fastest to demo, lower engineering lift, easiest A/B. Con: if they require data residency, won't work.
 - Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool): predictable throughput, good for scale and cost predictability. Con: procurement time + commitment.
 - Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem): best for strict compliance; longer lead time.

Cold email (subject line candidates)
 - "Quick idea to speed up Crestbridge kiosks by 2–3x"
 - "Pilot: low-effort AI assistant for in-store staff"
 - "Reduce kiosk search latency without re-indexing — 2-week pilot"

Outbound template (short)
 Hi Elena / Elena's inbox,

 Been following Crestbridge's in-store discovery beta — nice work. We help platforms like yours run inference for small, high-frequency queries (kiosk & staff tools) with predictable latency and cost.

 Quick idea: run a short pilot to route kiosk SKU queries to a lightweight model backed by our KV caching and batching — should cut P95 latency ~2–3x and reduce per-query cost. No major infra changes; we can run hosted or spin up a dedicated pool for predictable performance.

 Would you be open to 20 minutes next week to show a short demo?

 — Jordan

Phone / call opener (30s)
 - "Hi Elena — Jordan from Redwood. Quick one: we helped a regional grocer cut kiosk search latency in half and reduce ops overhead by using batching + prefix caching at the inference layer. Curious if your team would be interested in a 2‑week, low-commitment pilot to see similar gains?"

Objection handling (short bullets)
 - "We can't send PII to hosted services" -> offer Dedicated or Private; discuss token-level filters, acceptability of hashed identifiers, and enterprise contract.
 - "Procurement will take months" -> propose an internal pilot using hosted API or a small Dedicated PoC with a short-term commit; provide SOW template and T-shirt pricing for PoC.
 - "We're already testing vendor X" -> ask what's missing (latency/cost/ops), propose a focused A/B on the narrow kiosk flow where we expect wins.

Open questions to validate on discovery call
 - Catalog size (# SKUs), typical query length, and QPS for busy stores.
 - Current infra constraints (can they route traffic to an external endpoint?), required SLA/P95 targets.
 - Data classification: are queries considered PII or PHI? Encryption/KMS needs?
 - Who signs the SOW? procurement timeline?

Immediate next steps (what I should do)
 - Prep a 10-minute demo using a toy catalog (use internal sample + Redwood hosted endpoint) — target demo by Feb 12.
 - Ask Maya to draft a one-pager with pilot pricing (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
 - Get intro template approved by Ravi (legal/reg review link).
 - Reach out to Elena with two time options.

Notes to self / shorthand
 - Demo should emphasize P95 and cost per 1k queries. Bring concrete numbers from similar retail pilot we did (ask eng for previous deck).
 - Keep ask tiny: 2-week pilot, one store, staff-facing only, non-PII flow.
 - If they push for on-prem, escalate to solutions-eng early.

Related links / references
 - internal playground model config: /contrib/playbooks/retail-kiosk-demo (ask eng for path)
 - previous grocery pilot metrics (email thread)

Rough timeline idea for sales pitch
 - Week 0: kickoff + data sample exchange (1–2 days)
 - Week 1: integration + demo (hosted)
 - Week 2: run traffic, measure, tweak (A/B)
 - End Week 2: present results + discuss Dedicated/Private for roll.

Misc scratch lines (brain dump)
 - Could sell as co-sell with SI (they love low lift demos).
 - Pricing nudge: show savings in tokens + ops vs doing proprietary indexing work.
 - Keep internal note: capture exact SKUs per store — small catalogs behave differently.

-- end scratchpad --
